# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: Print + C0 control fixture  (issue #5, milestone 0.1.0)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/print_c0_spec.txt
#
# Evidence file for the implementer and the critic. Every case cites its source.
# It is test DATA, not a test: tests/print.rs + tests/common/mod.rs are written
# from it. Expected screens were produced by an independent Python model of xterm
# semantics and then cross-checked (64/64 cases) against a throw-away Rust probe
# that drives the real tessera-vt Parser and tessera-grid Grid using the
# "FIXED" design in DECISIONS below. The same probe run with the brief taken
# literally fails 4 cases (A06, G05, H05, H10): see "ISSUE TEXT CORRECTIONS".
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES
#   xterm ctlseqs   https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#                   (VT100 Mode > Single-character functions; SM/DECSET lists)
#   xterm source    https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots (master)
#                   charproc.c  dotext() WrapLine() CASE_BS CASE_TAB CASE_VMOT
#                               CASE_BELL CASE_SUB CASE_ENQ resetCharsets()
#                   cursor.c    CursorBack() CarriageReturn() xtermIndex()
#                   tabs.c      TabToNextStop()
#                   util.c      WriteText()  (INSERT -> InsertChar)
#                   VTPrsTbl.c  ansi_table[]  (ground-state action per byte)
#   DEC VT100 UG    https://vt100.net/docs/vt100-ug/chapter3.html  (3.3.1, Table 3-10)
#   DEC VT510 RM    https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECAWM.html
#                   https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/IRM.html
#   Alacritty       https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/master/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs
#                   (input, put_tab, backspace)
#   WezTerm         https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/main/term/src/terminalstate/
#                   performer.rs (Backspace, Linefeed, CarriageReturn), mod.rs (c0_horizontal_tab)
#   kitty           https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/master/kitty/screen.c
#                   (screen_tab writes tab markers into blank cells; kitty's pending-wrap model
#                   differs from the grid's, so it is not used as an oracle for pending-wrap rows)
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SCRIPT / STEP SYNTAX (what run_script must decode)
#   Escapes in `step:` payloads:  \xNN raw byte   \r \n \t   \\ backslash
#                                 \u{H..} one Unicode scalar, UTF-8 encoded
#                                 (needed for C1 controls: tessera-vt only sees U+0080..U+009F
#                                  as Execute when they arrive UTF-8 encoded)
#                                 everything else is literal. Payloads never contain '|' or a
#                                 trailing '\' as text.
#   step kinds:
#     feed <payload>             one Terminal::advance call with the decoded bytes
#     feed_bytewise <payload>    one advance call PER BYTE (chunk-boundary independence)
#     set auto_wrap true|false   Terminal::set_auto_wrap  (CSI ? 7 h/l arrives with #8)
#     set insert_mode true|false Terminal::set_insert_mode (CSI 4 h/l arrives with #8)
#   Steps run in order on one Terminal::new(rows, cols). Mode toggles cannot be written as
#   escape sequences in #5, so the script files need a harness-level directive, recommended:
#   a line `@set auto_wrap off` / `@set insert_mode on` between payload lines (see D6).
#
# SCREEN RENDERING (the string run_script returns / insta snapshots)
#   one line per grid row, top to bottom, each terminated by '\n':
#     1. cell chars, one per column (a blank cell is ' ')
#     2. if the cursor is on this row, insert '|' IMMEDIATELY AFTER the cursor's cell, i.e. at
#        string index cursor.col + 1.  (Cursor on blank col 0 of an empty row renders " |".)
#     3. strip trailing ' ' characters (after step 2, so '|' anchors the line)
#     4. if Line::wrapped, append '\'
#   Rows below are written with a leading '>' that is NOT part of the line (so empty rows and
#   leading blanks are unambiguous).  `cursor` is 0-based (row,col) = grid.cursor(); the issue
#   text quotes 1-based ("row 2 col 2" == (1,1)).  `pending_wrap` is grid.pending_wrap() and is
#   NOT visible in the render, so each case lists it explicitly (D6 recommends a footer line in
#   the snapshot so it is pinned too).  `scrollback` is what Grid::scrollback_len() /
#   scrollback_line(0) must report (text trimmed of trailing blanks, wrapped flag).
#
# TERMINAL DEFAULTS asserted by H08: auto_wrap() == true, insert_mode() == false.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first)
#   D1  HT while pending wrap is armed (A06).
#       xterm tabs.c TabToNextStop() and WezTerm c0_horizontal_tab() leave the pending flag
#       alone; Alacritty put_tab() wraps immediately; the brief's `grid.tab_forward(1)` CLEARS
#       it. Recommend xterm/WezTerm: in control::execute, `if grid.pending_wrap() { /* no-op:
#       pending implies cursor is on the last column, nothing to tab to */ } else {
#       grid.tab_forward(1) }`. Needs no grid change.
#   D2  IRM + pending wrap (H05, H10).  grid.insert_chars() clears pending_wrap, so the brief's
#       "Print first calls insert_chars(1)" inserts at the LAST column of the OLD row instead of
#       wrapping. xterm wraps first (dotext -> WrapLine, then WriteText -> InsertChar).
#       Recommend, using only the public grid API, when insert_mode && pending_wrap &&
#       auto_wrap: `let row = grid.cursor().row; grid.line_mut(row).unwrap().wrapped = true;
#       grid.carriage_return(); grid.line_feed();` and only then insert_chars(1) + put_char.
#       (Duplicates Grid::put_cell's wrap step; suggest a follow-up grid method
#       `resolve_pending_wrap()` owned by whoever next touches grid.rs.)  With auto_wrap off the
#       existing goto(row, cols-1) path is used and insert_chars(1) there just replaces the cell.
#   D3  SUB (0x1A) / CAN (0x18) in ground state (G04).  xterm (decTerminalID >= 100, the
#       default) PRINTS U+2592 (U+2426 for id > 200) for SUB; Alacritty, kitty, WezTerm ignore.
#       Recommend ignore (matches the brief). Only intentional xterm divergence here.
#   D4  C1 controls arrive as Action::Execute(0x80..=0x9F) (G06).  #5 ignores them as briefed;
#       whoever wires ESC D/E/H/M (IND/NEL/HTS/RI) should make Execute(0x84/0x85/0x88/0x8D) call
#       the same handlers so the two paths cannot drift. Not blocking #5.
#   D5  LNM (CSI 20 h) is not in the brief's API: LF/VT/FF never CR in #5 (E01 pins the default
#       'off' behaviour). #8 needs a `newline_mode` flag consumed by control::execute.
#   D6  Harness shape (the brief fixes only `run_script(bytes, rows, cols) -> String`).
#       Recommend: (a) append a footer `cursor=(r,c) pending_wrap=bool` to the snapshot text
#       because pending wrap is the point of this issue and the '|' cannot show it;
#       (b) script files hold `@set ...` directive lines for mode toggles plus a `@size RxC`
#       line, with a second helper `run_script_file(path) -> String` that parses them and calls
#       run_script's internals; (c) every script is executed twice, whole and byte-by-byte, and
#       both renders must be identical (case I01, any proptest); (d) the script-text decoder
#       must reject unknown escapes (panic) so typos do not silently print backslashes.
#   D7  Pending wrap across a DECAWM toggle (not a row; behaviour is not chunk-stable in xterm).
#       The grid always arms pending wrap, set_auto_wrap never touches it, and the NEXT print
#       applies the CURRENT mode (B03 pins on->off). off->on after an armed cell is left
#       unspecified/untested: xterm's own result depends on how the bytes were batched.
#   D8  Tab cells: xterm writes nothing for HT (D04); Alacritty/kitty record a tab marker in
#       blank cells for copy/paste. Recommend xterm. HTS/TBC are not wired in #5, so only the
#       default every-8 stops exist; reverse-wrap (DECSET 45/1045) is absent, matching xterm's
#       default (C01).
#
# ISSUE TEXT CORRECTIONS (verified)
#   1. "NUL/DEL ignored" under Action::Execute: DEL never arrives as Execute. tessera-vt emits
#      Action::Print('\u{7f}') (vte ground state; probed). Terminal's Print path must drop U+007F
#      (and defensively any char < 0x20) or DEL takes a cell and moves the cursor (G05). NUL does
#      arrive as Execute(0).
#   2. "HT -> tab_forward(1)" is not xterm-correct in the pending-wrap state (A06, D1).
#   3. "when set, a Print first calls grid.insert_chars(1)" is wrong in the pending-wrap state
#      (H05, H10, D2).
#   4. BEL "exactly once": the existing inline `Execute(0x07)` check in Terminal::advance must
#      move into control::execute, not be duplicated (F03). A BEL that terminates an OSC is
#      swallowed by the parser and must not ring (F04).
#   5. Done-when "cursor at row 2 col 2" is 1-based; Grid::cursor() is 0-based (1,1).
#   6. Existing snapshot dir already has keyboard__legacy_xterm_matrix.snap; insta will name the
#      new ones print__<name>.snap (tests/print.rs). G07/G08 rows (CSI/ESC/OSC/DCS ignored) are
#      correct for #5 only and must be deleted/rewritten by #6/#9.
# =============================================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A. DECAWM on (default): pending wrap

### A01_wrap_81_chars_80x3
size: 3x80
step: feed 01234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789X
cite: https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c dotext()/WrapLine(): do_wrap armed after col 80, next print sets LINEWRAPPED, CR+IND, then writes; https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECAWM.html
note: Headline case from the issue. 81st char lands at row 2 col 1 (1-based); row 1 wrapped; cursor row 2 col 2 (1-based) = (1,1) 0-based.
screen:
>01234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789\
>X |
>
cursor: (1,1)   # 1-based row 2 col 2
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
wrapped_rows(1-based): [1]

### A06_80_chars_then_HT_then_X_80x3

### A07_wrap_scrolls_at_bottom_3x5
size: 3x5
step: feed abcdefghijklmnop
cite: https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c WrapLine(): LINEWRAPPED set before xtermIndex(); scrolling moves the flag with the line
note: 16 chars into 3x5: the 16th wraps at the bottom row and scrolls. 'abcde' leaves the screen into scrollback (wrapped==true). Visible: fghij\ / klmno\ / p.
screen:
>fghij\
>klmno\
>p |
cursor: (2,1)   # 1-based row 3 col 2
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=1 first=("abcde", wrapped=true)
assert: scrollback_len == 1; scrollback[0] == ("abcde", wrapped=true)
wrapped_rows(1-based): [1, 2]

### D02_HT_from_col7_and_col8_1x24
size: 1x24
step: feed 1234567\tA\tB
cite: https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/tabs.c TabNext(): next stop STRICTLY greater than the cursor column
note: From index 7 -> 8; from index 8 (after A is written the cursor is at 9) -> 16. Cursor sitting exactly on a stop moves to the next one: covered by D03.
screen:
>1234567 A       B |
cursor: (0,17)   # 1-based row 1 col 18
pending_wrap: false
requests: []

### H10_insert_scrolling_wrap_2x4
size: 2x4
step: feed abcdefgh
step: set insert_mode true
step: feed X
cite: https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charproc.c dotext(): WrapLine() (scroll) then InsertChar
note: Pending at the bottom-right: wrap scrolls first, X lands at the start of the fresh bottom row. Visible: 'efgh\' / 'X'.

>efgh\
>X |
cursor: (1,1)   # 1-based row 2 col 2
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=1 first=("abcd", wrapped=true)
assert: scrollback_len == 1
wrapped_rows(1-based): [1]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- I. Chunking and non-ASCII

### I01_byte_by_byte_equals_one_shot_3x5
size: 3x5
step: feed_bytewise abcdefg\r\n\thi\x07
cite: tessera-vt Parser is incremental; Terminal::advance must be chunk-agnostic
note: Feeding one byte per advance() call must produce the same screen as a single call. The test should run EVERY case in this file both ways.
screen:
>fg
>    h\
>i |
cursor: (2,1)   # 1-based row 3 col 2
pending_wrap: false
requests: [Bell]
scrollback: len=1 first=("abcde", wrapped=true)
assert: requests == [Bell]
wrapped_rows(1-based): [2]

### I02_non_ascii_single_width_1x6

step: feed aéb
cite: tessera-vt Action::Print(char); wide/combining characters belong to #4 (grid unicode-width), out of scope
note: U+00E9 is one column wide: 'aéb' occupies three cells.

>aéb |
